assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental and conceptual demonstration that electrons tunnel over long distances through folded proteins, with rates governed by distance and the intervening medium (driving force, reorganization energy, coupling). Ru-modified proteins and the later hopping picture give a physically stated mechanism that underlies respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer, the physical-mechanism-in-biology kind of work I value most.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear core of the protein ET program, with a coherent two-person configuration. Contributions from others in the field (e.g. Dutton's work on natural systems, Marcus theory already recognized in 1992) must be acknowledged but do not displace this pair.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of kinetics, mutants and structures, independently confirmed; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier Marcus prize and with Dutton's contributions may make the committee ask what is new.
Whether the committee views this as a line of work rather than one discrete discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a central mechanism in respiration, photosynthesis and fuel catalysis. Concerted versus stepwise PCET, theory of vibronically nonadiabatic coupling and molecular electrocatalysts put proton and electron movement on a physical footing. Close to my own research but I weigh it on generality of the principle.
assessment.attribution: Mayer (thermochemical and mechanistic framework), Hammes-Schiffer (theory) and Nocera (PCET in proteins and water-splitting catalysts) are distinct, complementary contributions; Meyer is an early originator of the term and concept, so allocation of priority is a real question.
assessment.maturity: Principles are well established and widely used across chemistry and biochemistry, though some applied electrocatalysis claims remain debated.
uncertainties: Priority between Meyer, Nocera and Mayer is unresolved.
Part of the candidacy is a field rather than a single discovery; Nocera's catalyst claims were contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structures from micro-crystals before radiation damage and time-resolved structural movies of reactions. This makes dynamic chemical mechanisms visible, which fits the committee's interest in methods that reveal mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof of principle, Fromme (photosystem I nanocrystals) and Schlichting (time-resolved applications) are central; Hajdu's conceptual role is major but I am uncertain about his status, and Spence, Barty and others contributed, so a three-person limit is hard.
assessment.maturity: Method is validated across many facilities; the strongest chemical payoffs (time-resolved enzyme and photoreceptor dynamics) are still maturing and are not yet routine.
uncertainties: Large collaborative effort with contested credit.
Uncertain whether the science delivered matches the methodological promise; Hajdu's status unverified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase carries out biological N2 reduction with an unusual iron-molybdenum cofactor; structures (including the interstitial carbide) and mechanistic work address a foundational biochemical transformation with energy-conversion and metalloenzyme significance.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle provided the key structures, Seefeldt and Dean/Ribbe key biochemical and cofactor work; credit across five names is hard to fit in three, and the cofactor biosynthesis contributions are separate.
assessment.maturity: Structures are solid and independently reproduced, but the catalytic mechanism and the N2 binding state remain incompletely resolved, so recognition may be somewhat premature for a mechanism prize.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction still debated.
Allocation among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues has opened a new chemical modality with a mechanistic basis in induced proximity to E3 ligases, now in clinical trials. Impact on drug discovery is considerable.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept, Ciulli contributed structural and mechanistic design; Handa, Ito and others established cereblon as the thalidomide target, so up to eight names compete for three places.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging (no approved PROTAC yet as far as I know), so the timing may be early.
uncertainties: Eight credited names with a hard three-person limit.
Clinical outcomes not yet decisive; I cannot independently verify trial status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors use engineered deaminases to convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a chemically designed tool for genome editing with rapid uptake and early clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the decisive originator; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees on cytosine and adenine base editors. Whether the prize would go to Liu alone is open; Nishida and Kondo made an independent deaminase fusion.
assessment.maturity: Very recent (2016-2017) but quickly confirmed widely; a prize so soon after the 2020 CRISPR prize may be viewed as premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with CRISPR recognition and with prime editing of the same lab.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a general, mechanistically well-understood method used constantly in pharmaceutical synthesis; the ligand and mechanism work is clean and important.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled general amination; Migita and Kosugi's earlier tin amide chemistry is a priority question but not a general method.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely confirmed and used for decades; however, cross-coupling was recognized in 2010, which may count against a similar prize.
uncertainties: Committee may consider this too close to the 2010 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for membraneless compartments links physical chemistry to cell biology and has changed how cellular organization is conceived.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids; Rosen provided the multivalency framework, while Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physical principles.
assessment.maturity: The concept is widely adopted but the physiological relevance, definitions and mechanisms in cells remain contested, so maturity is limited.
uncertainties: Debated physiological significance and rigor of in vivo claims.
Mixture of concept and experimental discovery.
